newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firmer but volumes light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firmer but volumes light.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended slightly higher Monday, with the complex again failing to follow through to the downside, but volumes were very light, traders said.

"Gold is continuing to erode away in a very slow but steady fashion with most bullion dealers looking for $375 basis spot as their first downside target in coming weeks," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.

COMEX December gold ended up 40 cents at $379.60 an ounce, after seeing life-of-contract low last week at $377.70. In the bullion market, gold ended quoted $378.60/379.00 an ounce, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $378.70 and the New York close Friday at $378.00/378.50. Spot gold saw its lowest levels since March 1995 last week at $376.70.

COMEX December silver ended up 1.0 cents at $4.808 an ounce, seeing a three year low last week at $4.760. Spot silver saw an 18 month low last week at $4.760. The U.S. presidential elections Tuesday would likely overshadow further economic data due this week, analysts said. Last week October non-farm payrolls, October unemployment, and third quarter GDP growth data all suggested inflation remained little threat, disappointing the remaining gold bulls, analysts said.

"When it comes to 1997 more and more bullion dealers and producers are looking for lows around $350 an ounce basis spot gold at some point during the year," Arnold said. "It is significant that more and more big volume producer forward selling orders are building up above the $383-385 level," he said.

"The South Africans have been doing some rearranging of their hedged forward sales in recent weeks by fixing their dollar forward sales and leaving the rand exposure wide open, so any strong dollar rallies will be seized upon by the South Africans as a fresh forward selling opportunity."

"But many Australian producers, on the other hand, are happy to be forward sellers around $380-381 basis spot." The spot gold/silver ratio ended steady Monday at 78.80, testing the 18 month high seen last week at 78.90.

"Silver continues to be a very nervous market with shortcovering rallies increasingly running into fresh scale up selling from funds and bullion dealers alike," Arnold said. "But there has been surprisingly little producer selling below the $4.90 level basis spot."
NYMEX January platinum ended up 40 cents at $385.20 an ounce Monday, while NYMEX December palladium closed up $1.00 an ounce at $117.60.

Cash market platinum fell to a low of $370.00 last week, its lowest levels since January 1994, while spot palladium saw fresh three-and-a-half year lows at $114.00. --Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
